# infrawrench_service (Resource)

A service: a named set of resources across providers and accounts ("Checkout API" is fourteen resources on three providers), with who owns it, how critical it is, and the reliability objects that already exist on their own (SLOs, runbooks, an on-call schedule) linked to it. Scorecards (`infrawrench_scorecard`) grade every service against the organization's operational bar.

**Membership is managed by `rule` blocks.** A rule matches resources by provider tag, virtual tag or name, so a new resource tagged `service=checkout` joins without anybody editing the service; that is the Terraform-native way to say what belongs. Resources picked by hand and rule-matched resources excluded by hand are managed in the app, not here: this resource never sends them, so an apply leaves them as they are.

Every list here is authoritative: a write replaces the stored list with the configured one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "infrawrench_members" "lead" {
  email = "dana@example.com"
}

resource "infrawrench_slo" "checkout_availability" {
  name           = "Checkout availability"
  sli_kind       = "probe_availability"
  probe_id       = "3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-8e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
  target_percent = 99.9
}

# Everything tagged service=checkout belongs, on any provider, plus the
# AWS resources whose names start with checkout-. A resource created tomorrow
# with the tag joins without anyone editing this block.
resource "infrawrench_service" "checkout" {
  name        = "Checkout API"
  slug        = "checkout-api"
  description = "Cart, payment and order confirmation."
  tier        = 1
  owner_team  = "Payments"

  owner_user_ids      = [data.infrawrench_members.lead.members[0].id]
  on_call_schedule_id = "1f0c2b3a-4d5e-4f60-8a71-9b2c3d4e5f60" # an infrawrench_on_call_schedule
  slo_ids             = [infrawrench_slo.checkout_availability.id]

  monthly_budget  = 4000
  budget_currency = "USD"

  link {
    label = "Grafana dashboard"
    url   = "https://grafana.example.com/d/checkout"
  }
  link {
    label = "Repository"
    url   = "https://github.com/example/checkout"
  }

  rule {
    kind  = "tag"
    key   = "service"
    value = "checkout"
  }
  rule {
    kind       = "name"
    value      = "checkout-"
    name_match = "prefix"
    plugin_id  = "aws"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique in the organization; 1–120 characters.

### Optional

- `budget_currency` (String) ISO 4217 code for `monthly_budget`, upper case (`USD`, `EUR`). Required with a budget and rejected without one, since the server discards it.
- `description` (String) What the service is; 1–1000 characters.
- `link` (Block List) A dashboard, repository or document shown on the service page, in order. At most 20. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--link))
- `monthly_budget` (Number) Monthly budget in `budget_currency`, zero or more. The `cost_within_budget` scorecard check compares the last 30 days of member spend against it. Requires `budget_currency`.
- `on_call_schedule_id` (String) The `infrawrench_on_call_schedule` that answers for this service. The service page shows who is on call now, and the `has_on_call` scorecard check reads it.
- `owner_team` (String) Free-text owning team, 1–120 characters. Display only: alerts are never routed by it. Use `owner_user_ids` for owners that can be notified.
- `owner_user_ids` (Set of String) Owning organization members, by user id from the `infrawrench_members` data source. At most 20. Each must be a current member when the service is written.
- `rule` (Block List) A membership rule. A resource belongs when any rule matches it (or it was added by hand in the app). At most 20. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))
- `runbook_ids` (Set of String) Linked runbook ids, at most 50. Runbooks are written in the app; the `has_runbook` scorecard check reads them.
- `slo_ids` (Set of String) Linked `infrawrench_slo` ids, at most 50. The `slo_within_budget` scorecard check reads their error budgets.
- `slug` (String) The short name the CLI and URLs use, 1–64 lower-case letters, digits and dashes, not starting or ending with a dash; unique in the organization. Derived from the name when omitted (`Checkout API` becomes `checkout-api`) and then kept: renaming the service does not change it.
- `tier` (Number) Criticality, 1–4, 1 being the most critical: `1` customer-facing (an outage is an incident), `2` important, `3` internal tools, `4` experimental. Omit it for an untiered service. A scorecard's `applicable_tiers` selects services by this value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned service id. Use it, or the slug, with `terraform import`.

<a id="nestedblock--link"></a>
### Nested Schema for `link`

Required:

- `label` (String) Link text; 1–80 characters.
- `url` (String) An `http` or `https` URL; 1–2000 characters.


<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `kind` (String) One of `tag`, `virtual_tag`, `name`. `tag`: the resource carries provider tag `key` (with `value`, or any value when `value` is omitted); keys match case-insensitively, values exactly. `virtual_tag`: the organization's virtual tag `key` resolves to `value` on the resource's cost rows over the last 30 days, so it only matches resources with per-resource cost. `name`: the resource's display name matches `value` per `name_match`, case-insensitively.

Optional:

- `account_id` (String) Narrow the rule to one connected account, by id from the `infrawrench_accounts` data source.
- `key` (String) `tag` and `virtual_tag` only, and required there: the tag key (see `infrawrench_virtual_tag` for virtual tag keys); 1–256 characters.
- `name_match` (String) `name` only: one of `contains`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `exact`. Defaults to `contains`.
- `plugin_id` (String) Narrow the rule to one provider, by id from the `infrawrench_plugins` data source.
- `value` (String) `tag`: the exact value, or omit it for any value. `virtual_tag`: the value, required. `name`: the pattern, required. 1–256 characters.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id or by slug: the slug is in the output of `infrawrench services`,
# and the id is in its --json output.
terraform import infrawrench_service.example checkout-api
```
